title: The Close Call
logline: In a local cricket match an umpire has a fraction of a second to end someone's innings, and the whole ground waits in silence for the gap between seeing and deciding to close.
human_question: How much room is really there between something happening and a person's ruling on what it was?

situation.what_happens: A match runs through a tournament that matters to everyone playing in it. Most of it is routine. Several times in a match something happens too fast and too ambiguously to be certain about, an appeal goes up, and one person has to give an answer within about a second, in front of everybody, with no replay and nothing to revisit afterwards. The answer stands whatever it was, and the person who gave it has to keep standing there for the rest of the day among the people it went against.
situation.who_is_involved: The umpire, who is usually a local person known to both sides and not paid much; the players, for whom the tournament may be the largest thing in their year; the crowd, which has already decided; and the organisers, who have to keep the tournament running afterwards.
situation.what_is_at_stake: A player's innings, a team's match, and an umpire's standing in a place he still has to live in. In a tightly contested local tournament, real money and real grudges follow a bad decision.
situation.how_it_unfolds: A match begins and ends on a fixed day, and the difficult moments arrive unannounced and may not arrive at all. The pressures are the closeness of the game, the crowd, the light and what is riding on the result. It ends with a result, a dispute or a walk-off, and nobody, including the film, can arrange which.

concept_merge.why_together: C044 contributes the exact case: when the object is small, distant or dimly lit, or the attention or the base is weaker, it strikes late and there is no time left for anything after the response, so the process simply ends there with nothing lingering. It also carries the sources' all-or-nothing rule, that where there is not enough time for a full response the mind does not give a half one; it keeps checking, 'what is it, what is it', and drops back. C040 contributes the grading that decides which case a given appeal is, by size, light, nearness and lateness. C025 contributes the rule that decision and doubt cannot occupy the same moment. C029 and C009, folded in from IDEA-0080, contribute what is underneath: bare seeing carries only the seven universals and no verdict; receiving and investigating add landing, staying and settling; determining adds effort for the first time; and not one of those steps contains any wish to act. An umpire is the one person in ordinary life required to convert all of this into a public answer on demand.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: Put together they describe the difference between a decision and a verdict. The sources say the process runs its course and simply stops, with nothing left over; an umpire's ruling has exactly that shape and then has to be lived with by everybody for the rest of the day. The folded-in material adds the part a sports film would never reach for: the moment before the ruling contains no wish to act at all, so whatever the crowd reads into an umpire's face in that second, the sources place nothing of the kind there.

concept_links.why: The digest describes the two great-object processes: when the base, the object, the light or the attention is weaker, or the object is small, distant or dim, the form strikes two or three moments late, and the process ends at the seventh moment of impulsion with no registration, so nothing lingers afterwards [C044-P:L27-L33; C044-M:L3-L9]. The digest's 'all or nothing' point belongs to this film directly: if there is not enough time left, the mind gives no half-response; determining simply repeats and the mind drops back. Two limits are carried: the moment-counts are not measurable delays and must not be dramatised as timings or reaction speeds, which rules out slow motion offered as a view of the moment; and 'if you didn't really notice it, you aren't responsible' is not what the source says, since the slight-object teaching is about whether impulsion arises and not about excuses.

The digest gives the source's own reason for one of its exclusions: decision and doubt are opposed, so where one is present the other is not [C025-P:L69]. The visible pause before a ruling is where a crowd watches that exclusion resolve. The digest's warning that energy and decisiveness are not virtues in this framework keeps the film from turning a decisive umpire into a good man and a hesitant one into a weak one.

The digest grades objects by prominence, which it gives as size, light and nearness, and by how late they strike [C040-M:L5; C040-M:L7], which is why some appeals are obvious and some are agonising. The digest corrects the tempting reading: 'pay more attention and you will see more' is not quite the source's claim, since the grade is largely set by the object's own prominence and timing.

Folded in with IDEA-0080, and the digest's own story seed for this concept is an umpire at a local tournament deciding a close call. It reads the table as a sequence: bare seeing carries only the seven universals; receiving and investigating add applied thought, sustained thought and decision; the determining moment adds effort for the first time; and none of these contains any wish to act, which only arrives once the machinery has finished [C029-P:L31-L55]. Its guards are carried: this is not 'we have no free will', and the factor counts are a student's analytical aid, never measurements.

Folded in with IDEA-0080. The digest describes the rootless sensing layer as weak, needing a working sense, an object, a medium such as light and attention, and carrying no verdict of its own [C009-P:L85-L98], and makes the point the whole group rests on, that the same arrival can be followed by entirely different responses in different people. Two of the players, the umpire and the crowd all receive the same instant and disagree completely about it, which is the digest's claim with a ground and a scoreboard around it. The digest's guard against reading anyone's misfortune as deserved applies to the player given out as much as to anyone.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: When something is small, far off or badly lit it reaches the mind late, and the run from noticing to responding has less time to play out, ending with nothing left over to revisit. These texts also say that making up one's mind and real doubt cannot happen in the same moment, and that the machinery before the ruling carries no wish to act at all.
what_must_be_real: Real matches and real decisions, with no appeal re-enacted or re-run. The umpire's own account of how close calls are actually made must lead, and no slow motion may be used in a way that suggests the moment is something a person can consciously watch happen, which the sources deny. Nothing in the edit may turn a wrong call into a judgement on the person who made it.
position_hint: middle to late: it follows the film about the neutral machinery and precedes the films about a response being formed, because it is the point where the machinery is forced to produce a public answer. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: Sports-highlight editing flattening the film into a reflexes showcase.
Slow motion suggesting that the moment is something a person can watch happen, which the sources deny.
Losing the umpire's own account of the work in favour of drama.
Treating a decisive ruling as evidence of character, which the C025 digest rules out.
Leaving an umpire exposed in his own community after a disputed call is broadcast.
drop_if: No tournament or umpire allows genuine unscripted filming of real decisions.
The available matches are too low-stakes to carry real tension.
The umpire is unwilling to reflect on how close calls are actually made.
The film cannot protect him from consequences a broadcast dispute would bring.

connections.note: Takes in the doubt-into-decision strand and the C029 and C009 links: the neutral machinery beneath a public ruling, which carries no wish to act.
Both trace the line between something that barely registers and something that draws a full, decisive response.
Two fast rulings with nothing to revisit, one continuous and private, one single and watched by a crowd.

selection.reason: Used by EPD-0045, proposed by the C029 digest's own story seed, and strengthened by folding in IDEA-0080's account of the neutral machinery that carries no wish to act.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
